purpose: Record the decision about how the voice tier is driven, and what is now ready for it.

the_latency_problem.what_was_built_first: An adaptive caller whose brain is Gemini and whose voice is ElevenLabs TTS, plugged in behind the existing SpeechSynthesizer protocol.
the_latency_problem.why_it_is_wrong_for_voice: Every caller turn costs a planner round-trip before a single word is synthesised. On a text tier that is invisible; on a realtime phone call it is dead air, and dead air changes the agent's own turn-taking behaviour, so the harness would be measuring a conversation shape that no real call has.
the_latency_problem.what_campaign_1_did_instead: EVA drives an ElevenLabs conversational agent as the caller, talking to Samvaad speech-to-speech. The caller does its own turn-taking and barge-in natively, so latency is a property of the two live systems rather than of the harness.

decision.primary: EVA + ElevenLabs agent, speech-to-speech, for the bot-to-bot arms.
decision.kept_as_fallback: The Gemini-brain plus ElevenLabs-TTS path stays in the tree. It is scripted and deterministic, which the EVA caller is not, so it remains the right tool for reproducing one exact conversation during debugging.
decision.audit_finding_that_still_stands: Before this session the duplex caller's voice was macOS `say`, labelled in code as a local test fixture. Flat non-native prosody degrades Sarvam's ASR, so the agent would be penalised for mishearing speech no real customer produces. ElevenLabs now sits behind the same protocol as `local` and `sarvam`, selected with --caller-voice-provider.

where_execution_truth_comes_from: Not from EVA. EVA scores what was said and how the conversation behaved. The deployed agent calls our real HTTP tools regardless of what the harness believes, and the append-only journal remains the only proof that a write happened. The two are combined per call: EVA supplies EVA-A and EVA-X, the journal supplies the required-action verdict.
what_is_ready: scripts/build_eva_records.py converts campaign-2 benchmark scenarios into EVA dataset records, carrying the goal, persona, the full 26-field account ledger and the ground truth.
45 records generated for the Hindi and Hinglish development split across all 15 families.
EVA dry-run passes against the campaign-2 agent config using EVA's own virtualenv.
what_is_not_ready: The EVA caller is goal-driven, not scripted, so it cannot replay our exact caller turns. Ground truth transfers; the literal utterances do not. Voice results are therefore comparable to each other across BASE and IMPROVED, but never line-by-line against the chat tier.
The ElevenLabs caller agent needs re-provisioning against the campaign-2 persona set; the existing one is campaign 1's single smoke-test caller.
Per-run tool binding (open issue O1) is still unsolved, so voice runs share one ledger row exactly as the chat pilot does.
cost_note: Voice is metered at roughly 5 credits per short call, measured: one 19-second session moved the balance from 285 to 280. Chat is not metered. Fifteen-plus-fifteen voice therefore costs about 150 to 160 credits of the 485 available.
